blocks.text: Through desire, the one carried along moves outward.
blocks.directed: Through desire, the one carried along moves outward.

blocks.text: Congratulations, You’ve Reinstalled Wanting. Welcome Back to Saṃsāra.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, You’ve Reinstalled Wanting. Welcome Back to Saṃsāra.

blocks.text: Because after everything we’ve learned about the extraordinary nature of consciousness, Vasugupta brings us back to a very simple human predicament.
blocks.directed: Because after everything we’ve learned about the extraordinary nature of consciousness, Vasugupta brings us back to a very simple human predicament.

blocks.text: The entire cosmic drama begins again.
blocks.directed: The entire cosmic drama begins again.

blocks.text: Saṃvāhya — one who is carried along, conveyed or driven onward.
blocks.directed: Saṃvāhya — one who is carried along, conveyed or driven onward.

blocks.text: Now that last word is particularly important.
blocks.directed: Now that last word is particularly important.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja interprets this as the bound individual who is carried from one womb or embodied condition to another through the powers constituting conditioned existence.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja interprets this as the bound individual who is carried from one womb or embodied condition to another through the powers constituting conditioned existence.

blocks.text: And the powers carrying this individual include the kañcukas, mental faculties, senses, subtle elements and gross elements.
blocks.directed: And the powers carrying this individual include the kañcukas, mental faculties, senses, subtle elements and gross elements.

blocks.text: You’ve got the limited individual standing on the conveyor belt, looking around, asking:
blocks.directed: [short pause] You’ve got the limited individual standing on the conveyor belt, looking around, asking:
[short pause] “Have you recognised your true nature?”

blocks.text: Now that’s the traditional saṃsāric framework, not an empirically demonstrated mechanism of rebirth.
blocks.directed: Now that’s the traditional saṃsāric framework, not an empirically demonstrated mechanism of rebirth.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja’s philosophical explanation is very precise.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja’s philosophical explanation is very precise.

blocks.text: The primordial limitation of the individual.
blocks.directed: The primordial limitation of the individual.
[short pause] And specifically with the feeling:

blocks.text: Manyatā — considering, regarding, thinking oneself to be.
blocks.directed: Manyatā — considering, regarding, thinking oneself to be.

blocks.text: And from that fundamental orientation arises desire.
blocks.directed: And from that fundamental orientation arises desire.

blocks.text: “I cannot be fulfilled until something changes.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I cannot be fulfilled until something changes.”

blocks.text: And therefore consciousness becomes outwardly directed.
blocks.directed: And therefore consciousness becomes outwardly directed.

blocks.text: Trika doesn’t simply say that every ordinary preference is morally evil.
blocks.directed: Trika doesn’t simply say that every ordinary preference is morally evil.

blocks.text: Wanting a meal when you’re hungry is part of embodied life.
blocks.directed: Wanting a meal when you’re hungry is part of embodied life.

blocks.text: The deeper issue is the metaphysical identification through which the subject experiences itself as fundamentally deficient.
blocks.directed: The deeper issue is the metaphysical identification through which the subject experiences itself as fundamentally deficient.

blocks.text: The limited individual mistakes the acquisition of objects for the ultimate recovery of completeness.
blocks.directed: The limited individual mistakes the acquisition of objects for the ultimate recovery of completeness.

blocks.text: And this is where the whole system becomes remarkably coherent.
blocks.directed: And this is where the whole system becomes remarkably coherent.

blocks.text: Remember rāga among the five kañcukas?
blocks.directed: Remember rāga among the five kañcukas?

blocks.text: The supreme fullness of consciousness is experienced through the condition of lack.
blocks.directed: The supreme fullness of consciousness is experienced through the condition of lack.

blocks.text: And that apparent lack drives the individual outward.
blocks.directed: And that apparent lack drives the individual outward.

blocks.text: The person searches among objects for a completeness that, according to the doctrine, belongs to their own supreme conscious nature.
blocks.directed: The person searches among objects for a completeness that, according to the doctrine, belongs to their own supreme conscious nature.

blocks.text: Now imagine somebody convinced that happiness lies in obtaining one particular thing.
blocks.directed: Now imagine somebody convinced that happiness lies in obtaining one particular thing.

blocks.text: Or anxiety about losing what they’ve acquired.
blocks.directed: Or anxiety about losing what they’ve acquired.

blocks.text: Or comparison with somebody who has something better.
blocks.directed: Or comparison with somebody who has something better.

blocks.text: The problem isn’t necessarily the object.
blocks.directed: The problem isn’t necessarily the object.

blocks.text: It’s the structure of seeking completeness from something conceived as ultimately external.
blocks.directed: It’s the structure of seeking completeness from something conceived as ultimately external.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja is talking about this structure at a much deeper metaphysical level.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja is talking about this structure at a much deeper metaphysical level.

blocks.text: He describes the limited individual as becoming outwardly oriented precisely because they fail to recognise the inward reality of turya as their own Self.
blocks.directed: He describes the limited individual as becoming outwardly oriented precisely because they fail to recognise the inward reality of turya as their own Self.

blocks.text: He cites the Svacchandatantra and Kālikākrama on ignorance, desire, differentiated mental construction and the continuation of suffering. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He cites the Svacchandatantra and Kālikākrama on ignorance, desire, differentiated mental construction and the continuation of suffering. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: And here’s the beautiful philosophical reversal.
blocks.directed: And here’s the beautiful philosophical reversal.

blocks.text: The object may be perfectly ordinary.
blocks.directed: The object may be perfectly ordinary.

blocks.text: But the underlying mode of experience can differ radically.
blocks.directed: But the underlying mode of experience can differ radically.

blocks.text: One person encounters the object through the conviction:
blocks.directed: [short pause] One person encounters the object through the conviction:

blocks.text: “I am incomplete, and this thing must complete me.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am incomplete, and this thing must complete me.”

blocks.text: Another encounters it without mistaking the object for the ultimate source of fulfilment.
blocks.directed: Another encounters it without mistaking the object for the ultimate source of fulfilment.

blocks.text: The difference is not necessarily in the outward action.
blocks.directed: The difference is not necessarily in the outward action.

blocks.text: It’s in the fundamental identification of the subject.
blocks.directed: It’s in the fundamental identification of the subject.

blocks.text: And now Vasugupta gives us the solution.
blocks.directed: And now Vasugupta gives us the solution.

blocks.text: Not simply suppressing all desire by force.
blocks.directed: Not simply suppressing all desire by force.

blocks.text: Not constructing a new ego whose proudest achievement is having no desires.
blocks.directed: Not constructing a new ego whose proudest achievement is having no desires.

blocks.text: But the disclosure of fullness through stable recognition of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But the disclosure of fullness through stable recognition of consciousness.

blocks.text: And when that recognition becomes established, the condition of being the limited individual is said to dissolve.
blocks.directed: And when that recognition becomes established, the condition of being the limited individual is said to dissolve.

blocks.text: Because we’re about to have a sūtra involving the destruction of the jīva.
blocks.directed: Because we’re about to have a sūtra involving the destruction of the jīva.

blocks.text: This is about the end of a particular mode of self-identification.
blocks.directed: This is about the end of a particular mode of self-identification.
